title: Workspace becomes named registry grouping over repos; pointer removed
summary: DECISION (refactor ws-registry): The orchestrator moves from "workspace == single repo path" to a multi-workspace, multi-repo model. (1) A workspace is a first-class NAMED entity that GROUPS many repos { name -> repos[] }; it is a pure grouping/label and holds NO graph of its own. (2) Each repo keeps its own in-repo .graph exactly as today (the repo stays the graph-bearing unit; graph-store forWorkspace stays per-repo-path keyed) — no graph relocation. (3) The single global pointer file ~/.claude/orchestrator/workspace AND the process.cwd()-as-workspace fallback are REMOVED. Resolution flips to: cwd -> containing repo (walk up to .git or .graph) -> that repo's graph; plus a derived repo -> workspace reverse index for grouped/dashboard views. (4) workspaces.json evolves from a flat array of paths into a structured v2 registry { version:2, workspaces:{ name:{ repos:[] } } } with lazy idempotent v1->v2 migration on load (each old path becomes its own single-repo workspace, preserving today's semantics). Daemon already removed the global default in P3, so registeredWorkspaces() MUST keep returning a flat Set of repo paths to avoid breaking ~10 sweep/claim call sites. The single gated irreversible step is feature->main merge + daemon restart, taken only by the dispatcher.
